golden_set.question: What is a Piping and Instrumentation Diagram (P&ID)?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: A P&ID is a drawing that shows piping and communications as unscaled schematic lines along with control features as symbols, illustrating the functional relationships between piping, instrumentation, equipment, and controllers.

golden_set.question: Which engineering disciplines typically create P&IDs?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: P&IDs are commonly created by process engineers, controls engineers, and electrical engineers.

golden_set.question: What is the main purpose of a P&ID?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: To indicate whether devices are automatically controlled and, if so, how they are interlocked with instruments, conveying the interconnectivity of automated components.

golden_set.question: In the example P&ID (Figure 1), what two devices are shown interacting with each other?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: A sludge pump (P-4-3) and a solenoid valve (FV-4-3) that controls seal water to the pump's mechanical seals.

golden_set.question: According to the Figure 1 control description, under what conditions does valve FV-4-3 open and close?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: FV-4-3 opens when pump P-4-3 turns on, and closes when pump P-4-3 turns off.

golden_set.question: Why is the seal water on the sludge pump in Figure 1 controlled to only flow while the pump is running?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: To conserve water; the wiring from the motor starter (MS) to the solenoid (S) allows automated control so seal water only flows when the pump is operating.

golden_set.question: What is a Block Flow Diagram and at what stage of a project is it typically created?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: A block flow diagram shows the main processes as rectangles or circles connected by lines and arrows for the main flow paths. It's commonly made by a process engineer in the planning stage or early in design.

golden_set.question: What process is illustrated in the example Block Flow Diagram (Figure 2), and what is its cited source?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: It shows a water treatment system (influent flowing through a pressure tank, oxidizing filter, IX filter, disinfection, and then to the distribution system), sourced from an EPA report on arsenic removal from drinking water by ion exchange and activated alumina plants.

golden_set.question: What is a Process Flow Diagram (PFD)?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: A drawing created by process or mechanical engineers early in the design stage, showing piping lines and symbols for major components such as pumps, tanks, mixers, and flow meters, ideally with instrumentation identified.

golden_set.question: Who typically receives PFDs, and what do they do with them?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: PFDs are often given to electrical and controls engineers, who use them as CAD backgrounds and add control and communication details on top to create P&IDs.

golden_set.question: In Figure 4, how are motorized or automated valves visually indicated on the drawing?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: They are shown with an "M" inside a box.

golden_set.question: What is the purpose of a legend drawing in a project drawing set?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: It defines the symbols, abbreviations, line types, and shading used on the PFDs and P&IDs. Sometimes there is one common legend for both, and sometimes separate legends exist for PFDs and P&IDs.

golden_set.question: What is an Instrument Schematic, and how does it differ from a P&ID?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: An instrument schematic is a detailed drawing for one particular instrument, showing wiring details and control logic notes relevant only to that instrument. This differs from a P&ID, which shows the interconnectivity across multiple instruments, equipment, and panels.

golden_set.question: What instrument is depicted in the example Instrument Schematic (Figure 5)?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: A flow transmitter, showing its coil circuit and electrode circuit wiring along with power (120VAC) and signal (4-20mA analog) connections.

golden_set.question: What does a Wiring Diagram show, and how is it different from a P&ID?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: A wiring diagram shows circuit components as simplified shapes with power and signal wiring between devices, terminal blocks, and I/O cards. This differs from a P&ID, which shows pipes and the relative locations of instruments and equipment rather than wiring detail.

golden_set.question: Which three instruments are wired together in the example Wiring Diagram (Figure 6)?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: A pressure transmitter (PIT-3), a 24-volt level transmitter (LIT-6), and a 120-volt level transmitter (LIT-7).

golden_set.question: What is a SCADA Network Diagram and what does it depict?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Also called a SCADA architecture diagram, it is a block diagram showing the basic SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition) architecture and the communication channels between devices, controllers, and computers.

golden_set.question: How does a SCADA Network Diagram differ from a P&ID?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: A SCADA network diagram lacks the locations of instruments on the piping network and does not indicate control details, unlike a P&ID.

golden_set.question: In the example SCADA diagram (Figure 7), what method connects the remote stations to the control server?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Serial-based radio communication.

golden_set.question: What three types of logic diagrams are mentioned in the document?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Ladder logic diagrams, binary logic diagrams, and Boolean logic diagrams (also called relay logic diagrams).

golden_set.question: How do logic diagrams differ from P&IDs?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Logic diagrams convey control descriptions pictorially, but unlike P&IDs, they do not show the location of instruments on the piping and do not show communications wiring.

golden_set.question: In the example Ladder Logic Diagram (Figure 8), what conditions must be met for the valve to receive an open control signal?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Either Valve.HmiOpen or Valve.AutoOpen must be true, AND Valve.Block must equal zero, AND Valve.Interlocks must equal zero.

golden_set.question: What do the two Boolean logic diagrams in Figure 9 represent?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: The left diagram shows an alternate "A or B" logic using parallel switches, and the right diagram shows an alternate "A and B" logic using switches in series.

golden_set.question: Why are letter designations used on P&IDs instead of full text descriptions?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Because P&IDs are busy drawings with little space for lengthy descriptions and specifications, so letter abbreviations are used for device labels, control loops, and device functions instead.

golden_set.question: In the Figure 10 legend, what does the letter designation "PA" stand for?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Pressure Action.

golden_set.question: In the Figure 10 legend, what does "SH" stand for?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Signal High.

golden_set.question: In Figure 10, what causes pump P001 to start?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: The level sensor labeled 0011 sends a discrete signal that starts pump P001 when a high level is reached in the tank.

golden_set.question: In Figure 10, the letter "M" appears twice with different meanings. What are they?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: The "M1" label on the side of the tank refers to a Manway, while the "M" inside the circle near the pump refers to a Motor. The same letter can mean different things depending on context, so the design engineer must make sure this is clear or add clarifying notes.

golden_set.question: Which industry standard provides the letter designations referenced in Table 2 of the document?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: ISA 5.1.

golden_set.question: In the instrument tag abbreviation system shown in Figure 11, what does the first letter of a tag represent, and what do the subsequent letters represent?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: The first letter represents the row, which is the measured variable (e.g., Flow, Level, Pressure). Subsequent letters represent the columns, which are the instrument function (e.g., Transmitter, Indicator, Switch).

golden_set.question: What does the abbreviation "LS" mean according to Figure 11's instrument tag table?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Level Switch.

golden_set.question: Why might the abbreviation "LS" be ambiguous if someone referenced Table 2 instead of Figure 11?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Because in Table 2, LS could mean either "Level Switch" or "Level Stop," whereas Figure 11 defines LS specifically and only as "Level Switch."

golden_set.question: What is the instrument tag abbreviation for "Flow Transmitter"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: FT.

golden_set.question: What is the instrument tag abbreviation for "Pressure Indicating Transmitter"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: PIT.

golden_set.question: What is the instrument tag abbreviation for "Differential Pressure Recorder"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: PDR.

golden_set.question: What is the instrument tag abbreviation for "Temperature Controller"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: TC.

golden_set.question: What is the instrument tag abbreviation for "Level Alarm"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: LA.

golden_set.question: What is the instrument tag abbreviation for "Conductivity Element"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: CE.

golden_set.question: What measured variable does the row abbreviation "FF" represent in the instrument tag table?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Flow Ratio.

golden_set.question: What is the instrument tag abbreviation for "Vibration Switch"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: XVS.

golden_set.question: What measured variable does "XV" represent in the instrument tag table, and how does it differ from plain "X"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: "XV" represents Vibration, while "X" alone represents an Unclassified measured variable — they are distinct rows in the table despite both starting with X.

golden_set.question: Where are instrument control abbreviations typically placed relative to an instrument tag circle on a P&ID?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: To the upper right of the instrument tag circle.

golden_set.question: What does the instrument control abbreviation "HOA" stand for?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Hand/Off/Auto.

golden_set.question: What does "HOR" mean, and how is it different from "HOA"?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: HOR stands for Hand/Off/Remote. It is similar to HOA, except the device can be controlled remotely — either automatically or by a remote user through a control panel or HMI software — rather than through local automated controls.

golden_set.question: What does the abbreviation "MOA" stand for?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Manual/Off/Auto.

golden_set.question: What does "OSC" stand for in the instrument control abbreviations list?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Open/Stop/Closed.

golden_set.question: What does the abbreviation "S/LOS" stand for?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: Start/Lockout Stop.

golden_set.question: What is the simplest type of control device described in the document, and what are its two states?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: The O/O (On/Off) switch, which has only two states: On and Off.

golden_set.question: In the HOA selector switch example (Figure 14), what happens in each of its three positions?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: HAND turns the device on with no automated controls; OFF turns the device off with no automated controls; AUTO allows the device to be turned on and off automatically through automated controls.

golden_set.question: Who authored this P&ID training course, and what is its course number and PDH credit value?
golden_set.ground_truth_answer: The course was authored by Mark Ludwigson, P.E., PMP. It is Course 462, worth 4 PDH (4 hours) of credit.
